notes:
The request is real and vendored: `berlingo-knob`, evidence class DESIGN_STAGE_UNVERIFIED, a gear-shift knob measured with calipers and photographs and never printed. The fork is the request's own recorded uncertainty rather than an invented one -- the base-plate height is a photo estimate its notes give as +/-2 mm, and whether the sleeve's mouth seats on that plate or stops short of it is a decision nobody can make from the evidence, which is exactly ROADMAP.md 3.5's condition for exploring an alternative instead of guessing. So the shared root is the sleeve as drawn, `plate-seated` trusts the estimate and spends the whole 52 mm envelope on it, and `as-drawn` carries the ancestor forward unchanged as the fallback. The proposals and models were authored for this replay; no recorded run of a branched knob job exists in a form this pipeline can execute.

What this case exercises that nothing else in the repository does. Three formulations of one job through the real `design-tool branch`, `route`, `run` and `status`, with the shared half -- the brief, the requirements, the engagement length, the printer -- read from one `project.json` that no formulation rewrites, and every receipt under the formulation that produced it. Each freezes acceptance revision 1 and supersedes nothing, so neither sibling cuts a revision from the other. `plate-seated` builds a materially different solid; `as-drawn` builds one byte-identical to its parent's, which is the instant a review answer written for one formulation could bind the other and is the false pass ROADMAP.md 4.2 forbids -- the suite shows the two envelopes differ in nothing but the alternative id, carried directly and through the execution plan, and that the answer written for the root is refused next door. Then `as-drawn`'s model is revised after its run concluded, and its stored VERIFIED derives STALE while both its siblings stay current: Slice B's derived status on a real job rather than a constructed one.

It runs with `--no-render`, so no witness image exists and all three recorded judgements say so. A verification PASS may not carry missing evidence -- the schema refuses it -- so what carries the limitation is the status the pipeline derives from the answer, which says in its own words that nobody has seen this part.

And then somebody decides. `dispositions` is what ROADMAP.md 4.5 asks for and nothing in this repository had done: a job explored, compared, and then settled. `plate-seated` is preferred on USER_SELECTION and `as-drawn` is retained as the fallback on UNRESOLVED_EVIDENCE, and the two bases differ because the two decisions have different reasons -- one basis on both rows answers 'why keep a fallback' and answers 'why this one' not at all.

The comparison run immediately before reports `preference.admissible: false`, and it is worth being exact about why, because the first version of this note was not. It is NOT the rubric: the three formulations are indeed measured against different envelope expectations, but `_preference` never reaches that branch. It is NOT an unmeasurable deciding axis either: every `not_compared` row on this job is CONTEXT and none is DECIDING. What fires is the first branch -- `as-drawn` has no current verdict, because its model was revised after the run that verified it, so its mandatory verdict derives UNKNOWN_STALE. Preference is inadmissible because one of the two formulations being decided between cannot presently claim to have passed anything.

A decision is still correct there. The fallback is retained precisely for the case where the plate estimate is wrong, and a stale concept is the right thing to fall back to -- it would need re-verifying before it shipped, which is what STALE says. What may not happen is the decision claiming measured support the comparison refused to give; STRONGER_CONCEPT would have claimed exactly that.
